title: Windows itself
blurb: Activation, accounts, features, Windows tools and settings.

remedies.title: "Activate Windows" watermark or Windows isn't activated
remedies.why: Windows can't confirm its licence: new hardware (especially a new motherboard), a wrong edition, or a key that wasn't applied.

steps.text: Settings › System › Activation shows the state and error; run Troubleshoot there.
If you changed hardware, sign in with the Microsoft account that held the licence and choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".
Enter the product key from the purchase if you have one.

remedies.escalate: Work PCs activate through the organisation; tell IT the error code.

remedies.title: Turn Windows features on or off (Hyper-V, Sandbox, .NET 3.5, WSL)
remedies.why: Some Windows parts are off until you turn them on.

steps.text: Open Windows Features, tick the feature, OK, then restart if asked.
Optional features (fonts, language extras, tools): Settings › System › Optional features.
Hyper-V and Sandbox need Pro/Enterprise and virtualization turned on in the BIOS.

remedies.title: Home vs Pro: which Windows edition do I have?
remedies.why: Some features (BitLocker, Remote Desktop host, Group Policy) need Pro.

steps.text: Settings › System › About › Windows specifications › Edition.
Upgrade from Settings › System › Activation › Upgrade your edition of Windows.
Home has Device encryption instead of full BitLocker on many PCs.

remedies.title: Repair Windows without losing files or apps
remedies.why: Recent Windows 11 can reinstall itself over the top, keeping files, apps and settings.

steps.text: Settings › System › Recovery › Fix problems using Windows Update › Reinstall now.
Back up first, keep the PC plugged in; it takes about an hour.
Repair system files first if you haven't.

remedies.title: "Some settings are managed by your organisation"
symptoms: some settings are hidden or managed
remedies.why: Work policies (or leftover ones from an old workplace or a tool) lock settings.

steps.text: On a work PC, that's expected; ask IT.
See what's applied: Settings › Accounts › Access work or school, and run gpresult /r in Terminal.
On a personal PC, "tweak" apps sometimes set policies; their own undo option removes them.

remedies.escalate: IT owns policies on work devices.

remedies.title: Open a command prompt or PowerShell as administrator
remedies.why: Some fixes need an administrator command window.

steps.text: Right-click Start › Terminal (Admin), and approve the prompt.
Only paste commands from sources you trust; admin commands can change anything.

remedies.title: Turn off Copilot, widgets or other built-in extras
remedies.why: New Windows features can be hidden or removed if you don't want them.

steps.text: Taskbar settings: turn off Copilot, Widgets and Task view buttons.
Uninstall the Copilot app from Installed apps if your version lists it.
Recall (Copilot+ PCs): Settings › Privacy & security › Recall & snapshots.

remedies.escalate: On work PCs these are often set by IT.

remedies.title: Paste something I copied earlier (clipboard history)
remedies.why: Clipboard history keeps the last 25 items you copied.

steps.text: Turn it on, then press Windows+V to choose what to paste.

remedies.title: Free up space automatically with Storage Sense
remedies.why: Storage Sense deletes temporary files and old Recycle Bin items on a schedule.

steps.text: Turn on Storage Sense and set its schedule.
DeskMedic can also remind you when temporary files pass a size you choose (Settings › Medic assistant).

remedies.title: Stop tips, suggestions and "finish setting up your PC" screens
symptoms: lets finish setting up your device
remedies.why: Windows shows tips and setup reminders; they can be turned off.

steps.text: Settings › System › Notifications › Additional settings: untick the three suggestion boxes.
Settings › Privacy & security › General: turn off suggested content.

remedies.title: Remove apps that came with the PC
remedies.why: New PCs come with trials and extras that slow them down.

steps.text: Settings › Apps › Installed apps: uninstall trials (antivirus trials, games) you don't use.
Some antivirus trials need their own removal tool from the maker's site.
Keep drivers and the PC maker's update tool.

remedies.title: Windows picks the wrong time zone
remedies.why: Automatic time zone uses location; with location off or wrong, it guesses.

steps.text: Turn off "Set time zone automatically" and choose yours.
Or turn on location services so it can detect it.
Then sync the clock.
